column3: The Hebrew names the soul rather than heart.
The Hebrew pictures pride as height of the nose and leaves the object of seeking unnamed.
The Hebrew pictures his response to foes as puffing at them.
The Hebrew names his heart rather than simply himself.
The Hebrew explicitly describes drawing him into the net.
The Hebrew begins with singular descriptions of being crushed and bowed down; BSB starts with plural they.
The Hebrew presents hiding His face and not seeing with completed verbs; BSB uses present descriptions.
The Hebrew does not explicitly supply me as the object of calling to account, or never.
The Hebrew pictures putting it in His hand; BSB interprets repayment by His hand.
The Hebrew presents the nations perishing as completed; BSB uses perish.
The Hebrew has their heart in the singular; BSB uses hearts.
The Hebrew has a singular mortal from the earth; BSB says men of the earth.
